newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour won't privatise Channel 4, Post Office - source.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour won't privatise Channel 4, Post Office - source.

text.p: Britain's Labour Party would consider privatising the air traffic control service if it wins the May 1 election but would not sell off Channel 4 television or the Post Office, a Labour source said on Sunday.
"Air traffic control we're looking at," the source said. "On Channel 4, we say we're not going to privatise it and the Post Office we are not going to privatise either."
The ruling Conservative Party said in its election manifesto it would consider different options for privatising the mail service. It made no reference to the television channel.

The source also confirmed that Labour, if it won power, would set up a review of all government services, land and buildings. Sunday newspapers said that was with a view to selling assets worth billions of pounds.
"We are going to require all (government) departments to register by November all the assets they use...and investigate whether or not they are used effectively and efficiently," the source said.
Press reports had said Labour would embrace a policy of privatising remaining state assets in a break with the party's previous policies.

Labour finance spokesman Gordon Brown has come under pressure to explain how he would match the Conservatives' spending plans for the next two years, as he has pledged to do, without following their privatisation programme.
The Sunday Telegraph said Labour leader Tony Blair would stress in a speech to businessmen on Monday that his party would seek to leave economic activity to the private sector."

It said he would say: "Where there is no over-riding reason for preferring public provision of goods and services -- particularly where those services operate in a competitive market -- then the presumption should be that economic activity is best left to the private sector, with market forces being encouraged to operate."
The Sunday Times ran with the story that Labour will conduct an urgent review of the assets of all government departments, with a view to selling many of them off.

The Conservatives said the reports showed that Labour was now retreating. "The Labour Party have opposed each and every one of the privatisations which this government has brought forward over the past 18 years, said Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine.
"Now Mr Blair, the man who has put trust at the heart of this election, is casting aside his principles like ballast from his sinking balloon."
Labour has a lead of at least 20 points over the Conservatives in the opinion polls and looks set to take power for the first time since 1979.
